newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: U.S. Sloan group launches $120 million Africa fund.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sloan group launches $120 million Africa fund.

text.p: U.S.-based Sloan Financial Group, the world's largest black-owned financial services firm, said on Tuesday it had launched a $120 million private equity fund for investment in southern Africa.

Overseas Private Investment Corp (OPIC), a U.S. government agency, guaranteed $80 million of debt for the fund while other U.S. investors, including Citibank supplied the balance, Sloan said in a statement.
Sloan executive vice president Justin Beckett said the launch of the fund supported the group's view that southern Africa had attractive investment fundamentals.
He said the fund's black ownership uniquely positioned it for involvement in black economic empowerment deals.

Leon Liebenberg, general manager of Sloan unit New Africa Advisors, said the fund would invest $5 million to $20 million at a time in unlisted ventures across the Southern African Development Community region.
"We're obviously looking at deals right now and being very selective, because we only intend to end up doing 10 to 15 deals maximum," he told Reuters.
"The investments that we're looking at most seriously are in South Africa and the sectors vary from tourism to telecommunications."
He said the fund would target management buy-outs, expansions, non-core assets disposals, privatisations and multinational investments.
Investments would need to carry expected annual returns of 25 percent to 30 percent, Liebenberg said.
Liebenberg said OPIC participation carried with it caveats on certain investments but this was not expected to be a major stumbling block.

"With OPIC being a U.S. government agency...ideally our transactions should have some link to the U.S. I think they are grown up enough to realise that not everything complies with U.S. standards. I don't think it's going to be an impediment," he said.
Leibenberg said OPIC had only turned down three transactions within its roughly 33 international funds.
